tools.label: Typographic arrows:
n.dropwrong1: And what exactly is that supposed to do?
n.typo_done: Yes, yes, you already found that one. Stop rubbing it in.
h.none: No ideas right now. Odd: I usually have too many.
card.ch7.label: Chapter 7
card.ch7.title: Footnotes
end.ch7.title: End of Chapter 7
end.ch7.body:
The eraser is back with the Pencil, the door is free and the Narrator has received his first footnote of denial.
In Chapter 8 words change their meaning.
page.p23.title: History of GRAND ADVENTURE DELUXE
page.p23.body: GRAND ADVENTURE DELUXE was the most awaited game of 1996.¹ It was developed in just three days² by a team of experts.³
page.p23.n3: ³ (note set in 4-point type: too small to read)
page.p23.n3open: ³ The note is open. You go down through the floor of the room.
page.p23.margin: note 3 is where i lost my eraser
page.p24.title: Glossary of signs
page.p24.missing: *  asterisk — missing (it fell into a note)
page.p24.margin: an asterisk weighs more than you'd think
page.p25.title: Lost property
page.p25.intro: Items found inside the manual. The owner may collect them from this page.
page.p25.margin: it erases anything that's written. so, almost everything
n.i1: The Reading Room. The quietest place in the manual. Until you arrive.
p.i1: remember the favour? the first one is easy. i've lost my eraser.
n.i2: An eraser? A pencil with an eraser? That explains a lot.
p.i2: it fell into note 3, on page 23. footnotes are down below. under the floor.
n.i3: Footnotes aren't places. They're... notes. Small ones. At the bottom.
n.i4: See? Page 23: note 3 is so small you can't even read it. Let alone go in.
n.empty1: The Reading Room. People read in silence here. Except me.
n.empty2: Nothing there. Try reading something, for a change.
n.fempty1: We're at the bottom of the page. Everything is huge. Even the silence.
n.fempty2: Paper, paper, paper. Close up, a sheet is a desert.
n.page_wrong: Not on this page. Everything has its own: asterisks on page 24, lost property on page 25.
n.tool1: That arrow changes nothing. Try another illustration.
n.typo_spine: "Encyclopeda". An encyclopaedia missing a letter. Incomplete, like all encyclopaedias.
n.shelves1: Instruction books for games that never came out. A library of promises.
n.shelves2: Don't touch the red one. It's the manual for my manual.
n.lectern: The lectern. You rest the book on it and read. Revolutionary.
n.door_tag: The door is sealed with a Proofreader's label: [to be corrected]. It won't open while that's written there.
n.door_open: The chapter 8 door is free. The label is gone. How, I won't say.
n.hatch: The space for footnotes. It's empty. Notes usually go here. In small print.
n.note_big: You enlarged a footnote. To 72-point. Typesetters are weeping.
n.note_small: Back to 4-point. Illegible, as befits a footnote.
n.note_tiny: Note 3 is in 4-point type. An ant could just about fit. A small ant.
n.down1: The note opened like a trapdoor. Inside it's... down. Very far down.
n.f1: We're INSIDE note 3. Everything is enormous. Or we're tiny.
n.f2: Those are letters. As big as houses. And up there is the line separating the note from the text.
p.f1: the eraser is under that asterisk. asterisks always fall into notes.
n.letters1: Giant letters. An "e", a "t", an "a". Together they say nothing. Like many notes.
n.letters2: Don't climb the "t". It's more fragile than it looks.
n.asterisk: A fallen asterisk. It weighs a ton. In the world, at least. In the manual, who knows.
p.eraser: my eraser! take it. but don't leave it lying on the floor.
n.ast1: The asterisk is back in the Glossary of signs. And underneath there was... a pink eraser.
p.ast: there it is. take it to lost property, page 25. that's where things get collected.
p.er1: my eraser! i'll lend it to you. it erases anything that's written.
n.er1: Anything that's written? Even... me? I'm mostly written.
p.er2: the proofreader's labels too. go back up and try it on the door.
n.x1: The label is gone. The chapter 8 door is free.
n.x2: See? All according to plan. I have never got a single word wrong in my life.
p.x1: not me. i swear. i'm holding the eraser.
n.x4: Then who? Notes don't write themselves. ...Do they?
h.enter.1: The eraser is in note 3, on page 23. But the note is too small to get into.
h.enter.2: The typographic arrows can resize illustrations. Even a little number.
h.enter.3: Enlarge note 3 with ⤢, then drag it into the dotted space on the floor.
h.eraser.1: The eraser is under the giant asterisk. It needs moving.
h.eraser.2: Things from the world can be taken into the manual. Page 24 is missing exactly one asterisk.
h.eraser.3: Drag the asterisk to page 24, then the eraser to page 25 (Lost property).
h.exit.1: The door is blocked by the Proofreader's [to be corrected] label.
h.exit.2: The Pencil lent you her eraser: it erases what's written.
h.exit.3: Go back up using the sign, then drag the eraser from page 25 onto the door's label.
